Case study, Chrome extension

Screen Recorder (QA mode)

A Chrome extension that records a bug together with what a developer needs to reproduce it. I built it for my own bug reports, and anyone can install it in about 30 seconds.

Type
Chrome extension (Manifest V3), published on GitHub
Tech
JavaScript, chrome.desktopCapture, Cypress, Playwright, GitHub Actions
Dependencies
None
Tested against
A bug bench I built for it ↗ (opens in a new tab)
Download for Chrome ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Why I built it

I used a tool called Nimbus to record bugs for my reports. When it changed, I rebuilt the features I relied on in my own extension, and then added the ones I wanted.

  • Console logs and network requests recorded along with the video. No tool I had did that for me.
  • Test steps with Playwright selectors, so I don't have to repeat a test just to write its steps down.
  • Marking bugs on the video, which helps a lot with frontend issues.
  • Exporting only the audio, for example from a meeting.

What you get from one recording

  • A recording of your screen, a window or a single tab, with no time limit, no watermark and no account.
  • Console logs synced to the video, including uncaught exceptions.
  • Network requests, exported as a HAR file.
  • Numbered steps, recorded automatically from clicks, forms and page changes, including navigation inside single-page apps. Typed values are never logged.
  • A *.steps.md export in which each step has a paste-ready Cypress or Playwright selector, so the list can become the skeleton of a regression test.
  • Annotations drawn on the video while you record, and markers added with a keyboard shortcut.
  • The full report, filed directly as an issue in Jira Cloud or Linear.

How I tested it

I didn't want to check the recorder against whatever a real website happened to do that day. So I built a bug bench for it, a page that breaks on demand. It can return a 500 on a write, throw an uncaught exception, or send a response that says OK and means the opposite. Each failure is known in advance, so I can check the recording against it.

Open the bug bench ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Install it

  1. Download the zip from the latest release and unzip it.
  2. Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
  3. Choose Load unpacked and select the unzipped folder.

No store account and no build step.
